At that point it automatically unfolds into your natural grip, while you're already launching your angle 3; upward uppercut slice right through the target.

Operating the Hissatsu requires to reach into your pocket to get a full grip, then pulling it backwards away from your to get it out of your pocket, while doing the unfolding motion (which is assisted but still requires training to be pulled of in a stress situation). Once you have the blade open you are either use it for a direct or a side swiping stab, which requires precision, because you will only make contact with the point of your blade. The straight blade knifes require for any slicing motion to change your natural hand position into a tilt to guide the blade, which also requires skill for every strike; not just for hand movement, but body movement as well, because it is very easy to hold the knife towards the wrong angle and thereby making it rather useless.
